candidateTheory.name: Quantum error mitigation
candidateTheory.scope: Algorithms to estimate ideal/noiseless observables from noisy quantum-device experiments without necessarily encoding logical qubits; not equivalent to fault-tolerant error correction.
nonclaims: Different methods demand different noise models, device controls and sample overheads.
No guarantee of scalable or efficient mitigation for arbitrary noise and circuit depth.
The 2016 preprint date of one source is not certified as the earliest origin of all error mitigation.

versionedPrimarySource.authors: Kristan Temme, Sergey Bravyi, Jay M. Gambetta
versionedPrimarySource.title: Error mitigation for short-depth quantum circuits
versionedPrimarySource.reviewLevel: specific equation pages p2–3 visually inspected, not a comprehensive physical proof

formulaCandidates.name: Noise-scaled Richardson error-mitigation estimator
formulaCandidates.description: Noise-scaled, weighted extrapolation of measured expectation values toward the zero-noise value, assuming the noise-response function admits a controlled small-λ expansion.
assumptions: Noise strength λ can be controllably rescaled to c_j λ while the target ideal circuit stays unchanged.
Small effective expansion parameter such as N T λ and a suitable noise-independent generator/controlled series remainder in the original paper.
Weights satisfy sum_j gamma_j=1 and sum_j gamma_j c_j^k=0 for k=1,...,n; original printed Eq. (4) has inconsistent summation dummy-index lettering in its first equality, normalized here to j.
Finite shot noise and imperfect noise-model manipulation can increase uncertainty; the formal O(λ^{n+1}) cancellation concerns truncation bias, not arbitrary finite-data error.
variables: Ehat_K(c_j lambda): measured expectation estimate at scaled noise c_j λ
c_j: distinct positive scaling factors, c_0=1
gamma_j: real cancellation weights determined by moment constraints
formulaCandidates.regime: Source's short-depth/weak effective-noise setting; not general correction of arbitrary uncharacterized hardware errors.
formulaCandidates.units: Expectation values share the units of observable A; c_j, gamma_j are dimensionless; λ has the inverse units of the scaling convention for L.

sourceLocation.locator: Printed and PDF page 2, Eq. (3) with coefficient constraints Eq. (4); mathematically consistent dummy index used, with source typo noted.

formulaCandidates.name: Ideal circuit as signed mixture of noisy circuits
formulaCandidates.plain: U_beta = gamma_beta sum_{alpha in Omega_L} P_beta(alpha) sigma_beta(alpha) O_alpha
formulaCandidates.description: Quasi-probability representation of an ideal circuit channel as a signed, normalized weighted combination of implementable noisy circuit channels.
assumptions: Implementable noisy gate operations form a sufficiently expressive, well-characterized basis to represent required ideal gates and composed circuits.
P_beta(alpha) is a normalized, efficiently sampleable nonnegative distribution and sigma_beta(alpha) belongs to {+1,-1}.
gamma_beta≥1 is the sampling-overhead normalization from absolute signed coefficients, and sample complexity can grow quadratically with it.
This formal relation is not a claim that noise-free gates are physically produced, nor that model identification, state-preparation and measurement errors vanish.
variables: O_alpha: implementable noisy circuit channel indexed by alpha
Omega_L: set of length-L noisy operation sequences
P_beta(alpha): sampling probability for noisy circuit alpha
formulaCandidates.regime: Source's probabilistic cancellation scheme with known/characterized Markovian noisy operations, potentially substantial sampling overhead.
formulaCandidates.units: All superoperators and weights act on density operators; coefficients P, sigma, gamma are dimensionless.
